printed_headline_estimate: Out-of-scope omnibus chi-square tests only (N = 712 households: 353 Noèpé, 359 Kovié; p. 4): (1) water source type vs. distance (<500 m vs. >500 m): Kovié χ² = 155.23, p < 0.001, Cramer's V = 0.658; Noèpé χ² = 207.46, p < 0.001, V = 0.767 (p. 10, Table 3 text); (2) water source type vs. access time: Kovié χ² = 196.382, p < 0.001, V = 0.427; Noèpé χ² = 154.159, p < 0.001, V = 0.382 (p. 10, Fig. 4 text); (3) water source type vs. satisfaction with committee management: Kovié χ² = 27.653, p < 0.001, V = 0.278; Noèpé χ² = 18.819, p = 0.001, V = 0.231; Total χ² = 43.685, p = 0.000, V = 0.248 (pp. 11–12, Table 4); (4) water point type vs. dissatisfaction factors: Kovié χ² = 900,442, p = 0.000, V = 0.792; Noèpé χ² = 1,067,470, p = 0.000, V = 0.869 (p. 12, Table 5). No inferential test links a legal/governance/tariff rule exposure to a water access outcome.
publication_year_note: Primary journal volume/issue year printed on header and citation line is 2026 (Asian Journal of Water, Environment and Pollution. 2026;23(2):025380294; Volume 23 Issue 2 (2026)); article history on p. 1 also prints 'Published online: December 1, 2025'.
rationale: The full text (16 pages) reports a mixed-methods study of community water governance (CUE/CE and AUSEPA) in semi-urban Kovié and Noèpé, Togo (N = 712 surveyed households; 32 interviews; 6 focus groups). Although the study computes inferential statistics (Pearson chi-square tests of independence and Cramer's V), every inferential test cross-tabulates physical water source/infrastructure type (standpipes, private connections, cisterns, boreholes, Zego rice canal, Akatsè Dam) against physical distance to source (p. 10), collection travel time (p. 10), user satisfaction with management (pp. 11–12, Table 4), or type of reported complaint/problem (p. 12, Table 5). None of these multi-category infrastructure cross-tabulations tests a narrow Criterion 2 legal, administrative, governance-regime, tenure, or tariff rule exposure on household water service access, nor yields a directionally interpretable governance-to-access contrast. All discussions of legal/institutional rules, non-delegation by AUSEPA, nonpayment disconnections (88/238 private connections), unsubsidized connection fees (55,000–100,000 FCFA vs. 75,000 FCFA urban TdE fee), and standpipe tariffs (1,000 vs. 500 FCFA/m³) are purely descriptive or qualitative without inferential testing.
